cosy-lesson.title: The Power of Habits : Automating the Self

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: to introduce the topic and clarify key target vocabulary for the session.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Review the key vocabulary for this session below:

cosy-blockquote.p: Cue – an environmental or sensory trigger that signals the brain to activate an automated habit.

p.em: Example: A vibrating phone is a powerful cue that instantly triggers the routine of checking social media.

cosy-blockquote.p: Routine – the physical, mental, or emotional behavior that is performed automatically following a cue.

p.em: Example: Replacing your sweet snack routine with hot tea is an effective way to overwrite unhealthy habits.

cosy-blockquote.p: Reward – the positive feedback or neurochemical payoff that reinforces a specific behavior loop.

p.em: Example: The dopamine hit from scrolling through news is the primary reward that locks in the habit loop.

cosy-blockquote.p: Automation – the process of executing behavior patterns with minimal conscious effort or decision energy.

p.em: Example: Habits are the brain's mechanism of automation, saving valuable mental energy for complex tasks.

cosy-blockquote.p: Overwrite – to replace or rebuild an existing automated routine with a healthier, conscious choice.

p.em: Example: To break a bad habit, you must keep the same cue and reward, but actively overwrite the routine.

cosy-blockquote.p: Willpower – the mental capacity to control impulses, focus attention, and regulate behavior.

p.em: Example: Since willpower is easily depleted by stress, designing a supportive environment is far more reliable.

cosy-blockquote.p: Environmental priming – arranging one's surroundings to naturally trigger desired behaviors and block bad ones.

p.em: Example: Placing your book on your pillow in the morning is a simple form of environmental priming.

cosy-blockquote.p: Friction – any barrier, effort, or obstacle that increases the difficulty of performing an action.

p.em: Example: By adding physical friction-like hiding the remote control-you can dramatically reduce TV watching.

cosy-blockquote.p: Desensitization – the gradual reduction of emotional or neurochemical reactivity to a repetitive stimulus.

p.em: Example: Constant exposure to notification pings leads to sensory desensitization, making real-life conversations feel dull.

cosy-blockquote.p: Habituate – to make or become accustomed to a specific behavior or mental process over time.

p.em: Example: Once you habituate to drinking water in the morning, the behavior requires zero conscious effort.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: pair/group discussion on core session themes.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs or small breakout groups, discuss the following questions:

ol.li:
How can we identify our subtle environmental Cue before it triggers a destructive routine?
★ What is one sensory cue that instantly makes you feel hungry, stressed, or distracted?

Why is a rigid morning Routine so highly valued by elite athletes and successful professionals?
★ What is the absolute first thing you do immediately after waking up in the morning?

How does our subconscious confuse a temporary chemical Reward with genuine emotional fulfillment?
★ What is the most satisfying reward you look forward to after completing an exhausting workday?

How does the brain's reliance on behavioral Automation free up our cognitive energy for complex tasks?
★ What complex task at work have you successfully automated so that it requires minimal effort?

Why is it psychologically impossible to erase a habit, forcing us to Overwrite it instead?
★ Have you ever successfully overwritten an unhealthy habit with a highly productive one?

Under what daily circumstances is your conscious Willpower most likely to fail completely?
★ When in your day do you feel your focus and discipline are at their lowest point?

How can we leverage Environmental priming to make study sessions feel completely natural?
★ How have you designed your current workspace to minimize distractions and prime your focus?

How does adding a small amount of physical Friction help us break addictive behavior loops?
★ What is one app or website that you have added friction to (like logging out) to reduce your usage?

Does chronic exposure to high-speed digital entertainment cause a permanent Desensitization to boredom?
★ How do you handle moments of pure, quiet boredom when you don't have access to your devices?

How long does it typically take for a foreign language student to Habituate to a daily study routine?
★ What new habit are you currently trying to habituate into your weekly schedule?

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: collaborative task or visual analysis in pairs/groups.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs, work together on the following task:

cosy-blockquote.p: The Habit Redesign: Imagine you are presenting a self-improvement framework to a group of busy professionals. Guide them on how to overwrite a bad habit using at least one second conditional, one third conditional, and one mixed conditional.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: 1-on-1 guided visual description and task response with teacher.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Look at the prompt and discuss your response with your teacher:

cosy-blockquote.p: The Habit Redesign: Imagine you are presenting a self-improvement framework to a group of busy professionals. Guide them on how to overwrite a bad habit using at least one second conditional, one third conditional, and one mixed conditional.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: deeper debate and statement evaluation in pairs/groups.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs, debate and state whether you agree or disagree with these statements:

ol.li: If you identified every environmental Cue tomorrow, would you be able to control your impulses?
If your morning Routine were completely disrupted tomorrow, would you still have a productive day?
If we removed the immediate digital Reward , would we stop checking our phones altogether?
If our brains lost their capacity for behavioral Automation , would we find daily life exhausting today?
If you had to Overwrite your biggest professional habit today, which routine would you target first?
If you had not relied purely on conscious Willpower last year, would you have achieved your health goals?
If you had practiced Environmental priming in your previous home, would you be more organized today?
If they had added physical Friction to their spending habits years ago, would they have saved more money?
If you had not experienced sensory Desensitization , would you appreciate simple pleasures more today?
If you managed to Habituate to reading every night, would your focus be significantly stronger today?

ul.li: Incorrect: I have a habit to check my phone → Correct: I have a habit of checking my phone / I am in the habit of checking my phone ((Grammar structure: use 'habit of' followed by a gerund [-ing] instead of the infinitive 'to check'))

Incorrect: It is more easy to build habits → Correct: It is easier to build habits / It is much easier to build habits ((Comparative syntax: 'easy' is a short adjective; its comparative form is 'easier', not 'more easy'))
Incorrect: We discussed about our routines → Correct: We discussed our routines / had a discussion about our routines ((Transitive verb: the verb 'discuss' takes a direct object without 'about'))

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Reflection & Feedback: Review language highlights and key corrections with your teacher.
